blind_target.title: Primed lexical decisions: Combined effects of the proportion of related prime-target pairs and the stimulus-onset asynchrony of prime and target.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We also attempted to replicate the well-established associative-priming effect using a visual lexical decision task (e.g., de Groot, 1984, 1987; Neely, 1967, 1977).
blind_target.outcome_quote: The fact that we were able to replicate the robust associative-priming effect demonstrates that our participants were sufficiently motivated and illustrates that if an effect exists, our Bayesian methodology enables one to find evidence in its favor.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors state the verdict for this target or the expressly named effect set.

luna_triage.reason: The paper says the associative-priming task was included to confirm reliability of its experimental procedure, including statistical methodology and participant seriousness. It reports a broad associative-priming effect and cites these works as examples; it does not state that it retests a specific finding from this particular cited paper. Prior adjudication: none.
luna_triage.location: Introduction, paragraph describing the additional associative-priming task; cited work identity in References.
luna_triage.omission_quote:
We also attempted to replicate the well-established associative-priming effect using a
visual lexical decision task (e.g., de Groot, 1984, 1987; Neely, 1967, 1977). This task was
included to confirm the reliability of our experimental procedure, such as the statistical
methodology and the seriousness of the participants.
